paragraph: Rutherford's single-family market is the volume story with 53 sales over six months at a median of $850,000, and the typical sale is a four-bedroom colonial with two full baths. A median of 17 days on market and 57 percent of homes selling above asking tell you it's competitive, though the sale-to-list ratio of 1.007 says buyers aren't being pushed far past list. Expect competition on the good ones. The monthly series tracks the normal seasonal arc, with closings building from 4 in February to 17 in June and 12 in July. The median eased from around $1,000,000 in May to $837,500 in July while volume climbed, which reads as a mix shift toward more mid-range houses rather than falling values. Two-families and small multi-families are a real segment here, 10 sales at a median of $940,000, and they sit at a median of 50 days on market, so sellers there are okay waiting for the right buyer. Condos and townhouses are mostly one-bedroom units, 12 sales at a median of $422,500, with a ratio slightly below list and about 40 days on market. Co-ops are thin at 6 sales and a median of $203,250, and they carry board approval, financing restrictions, and resale friction that not every buyer is aware of going in. If you're comparing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family, the rental income of a two-family, the low-maintenance lifestyle of a condo, or the lower price point of a co-op.
